speakers: Brad Gerstner (Altimeter, public and venture investor)
summary:
BG2 episode (Jan 2025): Gerstner walks through his annual outlook: high valuations, big-tech capex, AI compute demand, inference scaling, 10-year yield rise, fiscal/DOGE cuts, AI regulation.
Approach: concentrated net-long growth investor who sizes exposure by entry price and the 'boogeyman' (rates, inflation, deficits).
Main view: AI capex is real and compute constrained; rates above 5% or no spending cuts are the key risk.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: I try to put myself in the shoes of where I think the world will be in December of the following year
claims.claim: Annual process: review errors and omissions, forecast where the world will be next December, journal independently and have each team member do the same before setting starting positions.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: valuations Bill are quite High relative to where we started 23 and relative to where we started 24
claims.claim: Valuations are high relative to the start of 2023 and 2024, so the world already assumes things get better; the 'boogeyman' is inflation and higher rates combined with high valuations.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: we've seen the 10year go up almost 100 basis points and you know people didn't expect that
claims.claim: The 10-year yield rose almost 100bp while the Fed was cutting, the opposite of the housing and economic tailwind expected.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: the S&P 500 recently peaked at a about 22 times so in in 20 Q4 21 it was about 22 times earnings it troughed in 22 at 16 times and now we're at 23 times
claims.claim: S&P 500 forward P/E 23x vs 22x peak (Q4 2021) and 16x trough in 2022; big tech 21-23x (Nvidia 36x from 66x peak): not a bubble if growth expectations are met but less attractive than start of 2023 or 2024.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: so in this case Microsoft meta Nvidia Amazon and Google grew earnings at 44%
claims.claim: In 2024 mag-5 earnings grew 44% while the other 495 S&P companies grew 2%; consensus 2025 expects mag-5 21% and the rest 11%.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: if those earnings aren't delivered if you don't see this acceleration in nonch earnings in the S&P 500
claims.claim: The market needs a non-tech earnings acceleration (health care +4% to +20%, industrials -4% to +16%, materials -10% to +17%, partly tax cuts) and 10y yields below 5% to reach 10-15%.
claims.conditions: if earnings disappoint or yields exceed 5%

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: combined capex of Google meta Amazon Microsoft Apple and Oracle
claims.claim: Big-tech capex rose from about 160bn to 260bn in 2024, absorbing most incremental free cash flow, and is forecast to keep growing.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: inference is about ready because of chain of reasoning
claims.claim: Reasoning (chain of thought) models make inference demand jump enormously; Jensen expects inference to rise by 100,000x to a billion x, which requires new compute build-out.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: you can make an offensive bet that this will drive future Revenue growth or profit growth
claims.claim: Big-tech capex is either an offensive bet or a defensive prisoner's dilemma; the wall of worry about returns caps multiples.
claims.indicator: capex as % of revenue and free cash flow

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: the goal is the least amount of money in for the most amount of money out
claims.claim: Returns on incremental capital have fallen after a decade of super high returns; investors must believe in a 'pot of gold' like Google and AWS early investments.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: 100% of incremental free cash flow is now spoken for
claims.claim: A decade of unprecedented mag-7 free cash flow now goes to capex; what matters per Mike Mauboussin is return on incremental investment.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: the consensus forecast of all 26 of them missed by 80%
claims.claim: In 2023 all 26 analysts covering Nvidia missed by 80%; at the start of a phase shift linear modeling fails, giving early investors an advantage (Silicon Valley proximity).
claims.conditions: first 3-4 years of a technological phase shift

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: we just don't have a compute infrastructure in 2024 that kept up with it
claims.claim: Compute shortage persists: 300 million weekly ChatGPT users and inference-time compute hogs mean 2025 spending will still not create a surplus.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: I don't think that you can go out and spend and not have a business model to support the spend
claims.claim: Frontier labs need robust revenue (OpenAI about 4-5bn run-rate growing triple digits); smaller model companies have conceded they cannot keep up.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: we started 2023 with 95% you know 95% net long
claims.claim: Altimeter started 2023 about 95% net long and 2024 around 80% net long (longs minus shorts), reducing 'chips on the table' because the price of entry is higher.
claims.direction: reduce net exposure when valuation high

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: the most important thing in investing is the price of Entry
claims.claim: Price of entry is the most important thing (Buffett/Munger); higher entry price lowers variant perception.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: there's going to be a lot of FX headwind okay so the strength of the Dollar's gone up a lot
claims.claim: Stronger dollar creates revenue headwinds for mega caps with non-US revenue while capex rises, a Q1 2025 headwind.
claims.indicator: USD strength vs mega cap revenue

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: every time you have to re-calibrate based upon the facts on the field
claims.claim: Nvidia rose because earnings rose; consensus data center revenue of about 61bn in 2023 to near 200bn in 2025, a 60bn rise equal to hyperscaler capex increases.
claims.indicator: Nvidia data center revenue vs hyperscaler capex

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: intel was down over 20% AMD I think was down on the year
claims.claim: Semiconductor returns diverged: Nvidia +140-150% while Intel and AMD fell; AI beneficiaries are concentrated, with memory (SK Hynix, Micron) seen as a bottleneck.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: we think this has become a way way more sophisticated product lots of software baked into it that this is secular not cyclical
claims.claim: SK Hynix at about 6x forward earnings is priced as cyclical commodity memory; the thesis is secular demand, with rerating potential.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: we are power limited
claims.claim: Power is the binding constraint on data center build-out; China builds 100x more power; regulatory relief and extending Diablo Canyon matter.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: we tend to just take bigger bets on our best ideas rather than diversifying out into these other things that we know less about
claims.claim: Altimeter avoids derivative plays (power companies) in favour of bigger bets on the best idea (essentialism).

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: the expectation in the world now has gone from a lot of rate cuts to only one rate cut
claims.claim: 10-year about 4.7% and market pricing of cuts fell to one; Trump tax cuts (400bn annual stimulus) and deregulation raise inflation worries even as core PCE falls (shelter), so rates stay higher.
claims.indicator: 10y yield, fed funds futures, core PCE

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: I'll believe it when I see it
claims.claim: The market doubts Congress will cut spending to offset ~400bn of tax stimulus (no evidence in 5-10 years), keeping the 10-year elevated.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: if the 10e goes to 525 or 55 bill it's going to be an anchor on the stock market
claims.claim: If DOGE and Congress cut hundreds of billions, the 10y falls and equities run; if yields reach 5.25-5.5% it is an anchor on stocks and the economy.
claims.direction: long equities if yield falls; short if above 5.25

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: we grew every category roughly at 2 and a half per
claims.claim: Federal spending at 2019 baseline grown 2.5% a year would be about 5.0 trillion vs actual 6.7 trillion in 2024, a 1.7 trillion gap suggesting room for cuts.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: there is a global demographic problem
claims.claim: Aging populations shrink the taxpaying share; without efficiency (AI) or reduced benefits, bond vigilantes may push rates up if fiscal path looks unstable.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: it is just not that hard to get to a balanced budget at $6 trillion
claims.claim: Balanced budget is attainable at 6 trillion with tax-cut growth acceleration and AI productivity; the US is in a strong position relative to Europe.

claims.speaker: Bill
claims.quote: the people pushing for this regulation have moved underground to a certain extent
claims.claim: AI regulation risk moved to states (about 25 initiatives, Texas bill); a state patchwork would hand China an advantage and favour regulatory capture.

claims.speaker: Bill
claims.quote: I think you're going to see in 2025 a lot more companies open source
claims.claim: Expect more open-sourcing of models in 2025 after fears about regulatory capture.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: they are facing the largest innovators dilemma in the history
claims.claim: Google faces an innovator's dilemma replacing a 99% margin search monopoly; Gemini integrated with Android and Google assets could be strong, but margins will be lower.

claims.speaker: Bill
claims.quote: the concerns about running out of data the concerns about maybe there's a parameter limit
claims.claim: xAI's largest cluster tests the pre-training scaling argument; outcomes in H1 2025 (Grok 3) would be a new data point.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: what I'm most convicted in is that these guys are going to spend a lot of money on gpus
claims.claim: Large coherent clusters can be reused for reasoning training and inference, so GPU spending continues as workloads move to accelerated compute.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: the amount of capital that it takes to do these things is not the domain of venture capitalists
claims.claim: AI labs needed hyperscaler capital, producing partial ownership by Google, Amazon and Microsoft; competition and co-opetition are aggressive.

claims.speaker: Bill
claims.quote: we have printing presses we have companies generating enough cash flow to invest this much money
claims.claim: Nearly 300bn of corporate R&D/capex is bullish for US strategic position, answering earlier criticism about buybacks.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: reasoning models can get better just because you throw more compute at them as well
claims.claim: Reasoning models scale with test-time compute; labs say they are around the 'GPT-2' stage of log scaling, with big gains expected in 2025-2026; falling compute prices encourage more passes.

claims.speaker: Brad
claims.quote: you're going to see um real coding agents baked by Google and by open AI
claims.claim: Expect coding agents in 2025 to be meaningfully better, then consumer agents with memory and actions as reasoning models improve; use case expands from researchers.

claims.speaker: Bill
claims.quote: I'm not a fan of of macroanalysis and that I think it falls in the too hard bucket
claims.claim: Bill considers macro analysis too hard because of too many variables.
